title: Glazing a Small Bowl
story: Hana had shaped the bowl on Tuesday, but she waited until it was fully dry before glazing it. The pale coat looked thin, so she brushed a second layer around the rim and left the base clear. Her instructor said the clear base would stop the bowl from sticking in the kiln. She wrote the firing date on a card and set it on the shelf.

vocabulary.definition: Putting a glassy coat on clay before it is fired.
Light in colour, not deep or strong.
The edge around the top of a bowl.
A teacher who guides a practical skill.
A very hot oven used to harden clay.
Baking clay at a very high temperature.

options: The first coat looked too thin
The instructor told her to soak the bowl

quiz.question: What risk would a glazed base create?
options: The bowl might stick inside the kiln
The rim would stay pale forever
The date card would fall off
The clay would never dry
quiz.correctAnswer: The bowl might stick inside the kiln
quiz.explanation: A clear base is what stops the bowl from sticking, so glaze on the base would risk that problem.
quiz.supportingSentence: Her instructor said the clear base would stop the bowl from sticking in the kiln.

The top edge of a bowl
A card used for dates
quiz.correctAnswer: A very hot oven for clay

quiz.supportingSentence: Her instructor said the clear base would stop the bowl from sticking in the kiln.
